messages:
ravi: Quick perf note — ran fused-paged-attn (warpflow pipe-tiler) on A100-80GB, seq=1k, batch=4. Observed memory-bandwidth saturation and lot of SM bank conflicts when tile=64.
maya: Can you paste the perf command and the profiler flame please?
ravi: Sure — command:
```
./bench_attn --model=flashv4_paged --seq=1024 --batch=4 --tiler=pipe --tile_size=64 --kv-prefetch=on
```
ravi: nvprof shows sustained mem BW ~ 680 GB/s (device rated 1550GB/s), occupancy ~ 60%, smem usage high, ~ bank_conflicts spike at attn_kern.cu:456
sam: Hmm, 680GB/s is high but not full. Bank conflicts explain stalls. Did you try tile_size=32 or enable bank-aware tiling?
ravi: Tried tile_size=32 -> latency down 12% and BW drops to ~520GB/s, conflicts decrease. But overall token/sec only improves 6% (tradeoff with more kernel launches).
kevin: Could be KV prefetch thrashing L1/SMem. What's the KV cache hit pattern? Any evictions?
ravi: KV hit rate was ~0.87 overall, but for longer contexts (>512) we see bursts of prefetch evictions aligned with pipeline stage boundary.
maya: Did you profile shared memory reads/writes per thread? Also try enabling two-stage pipeline (prefetch then compute) instead of fused pipeline — may reduce cross-stage pressure.
ravi: Good idea. I ran a two-stage pipeline patch locally — results: conflicts drop 40%, occupancy drops to 50% but end-to-end latency stable and throughput +9% for seq=1024.
ci-bot: deploy-bench: run finished on scale-2 cluster, artifact: https://ci.redwood/bench/1970012345
sam: Nice. Might be worth adding a small heuristic: if seq>768 and tile>=64 then prefer two-stage tiler and reduce kv_prefetch concurrency to 0.5x.
kevin: Agree. Also try bank-aware indexing (pad smem per row by 1) and measure effect. Padding often reduces conflict noise.
ravi: I'll push a branch with two-stage + pad-smem + tile=32/64 arm and run full profiles overnight. Will post logs in the morning.
maya: Awesome — also add a perf/regression check so we can auto-detect BW saturation and fallback to safe tiler.
sam: +1 :thumbsup:
ravi: Filing followup issue: https://redwood.atlassian/browse/ENGRT-998 — notes + next steps.
kevin: Thanks — if overnight runs look good we should include as default heuristic in 0.12.0.
